_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-06 · SkyPlan — the $50k tab's real measure found: how much of the work sitting in students' CPL Plans a college has actually worked.
_status: Today was about finding the right thing to measure on the $50k tab before redesigning it. Sam supplied a MAP export with one row per student per credit recommendation — and it carries the piece that was missing: whether the college has acted on each recommendation. Statewide, 81% of them have never been touched. The measure that comes out of it — the share of a college's recommendations that carry any decision, including 'not applicable' — is the first one that matches Sam's own read of which colleges are good at this (Moreno Valley, Cabrillo, Bakersfield all near the top; the typical college sits at 5%). It's also the fair one: Cabrillo ruled out 844 recommendations and applied 320, and a cruder measure would have scored that as failure. Two other things landed: student headcount is finally out of the funding model everywhere it decided money, and the noncredit split now uses noncredit FTES. The tab redesign itself is next. Separately, GitHub had an Actions outage all afternoon, so everything merged today publishes to the live site once that clears — nothing is lost.

items.text: 🎯 NEXT — REBUILD THE $50k TAB on the new measure. Replace the three bare checkmarks with a stage per priority, each shown as a fraction ("412 of 1,847 recommendations decided") rather than a tick — a tick becomes the new finish line, which is exactly how colleges came to believe uploading a JST was the whole job. Show each college its own numbers only; never a league table.

⭐ REFRAME THE VETERAN STAR rather than repeating it. A college can earn the star without ever articulating a single credit recommendation. Pair it with what it produced: "979 JSTs uploaded — those generated 18,264 credit recommendations, none articulated yet. The star is the starting line."

✅ A FREE WIN worth raising with Malone — 11,495 rows in students' plans say "Credit Is Not Recommended". ACE is stating outright that no credit exists, so no college can ever act on them, yet they sit in every queue looking like work. Marking them not-applicable automatically would shrink every college's list overnight with no judgement call.

🎯 WHERE TO POINT COLLEGES — just 20 military training documents account for about 40% of the 424,945 untouched recommendations statewide. A push on those few would move more than a broad ask ever could.

🔌 WIRE MALONE'S NEW REPORT when it lands (expected 8/7). Three small steps: add the view to the daily pull, name it in the new builder, and add the builder to the daily job. Then this stops being a one-time file and refreshes every morning.

❓ ONE NUMBER NEEDED from MVC or Bakersfield — roughly how long does an Academic Records Evaluator take to work through one veteran's list of credit recommendations? That turns a college's backlog into hours, and hours into "your $50,000 covers it" — which is the whole point of the grant and the tab never says so.

🏗 BUILD THE NONCREDIT FLOOR. Switching the split to noncredit FTES only moved Calbright from $33K to $40K — the floor is what actually delivers the fairness Sam wanted (about $161K). Worth choosing the floor amount deliberately: with only four recipients, a $150K floor commits 60% of the $1M.

🔍 ASK MALONE ABOUT CALBRIGHT'S NONCREDIT FTES. The reported 21,438 works out to 8.6 full-time-equivalent years per student, which isn't possible — it looks like a count of enrollments. A placeholder of 1,000 is in place and clearly marked; a real figure replaces it automatically.

⏳ GITHUB OUTAGE (8/6 afternoon) — GitHub confirmed an Actions incident: jobs weren't getting machines and pushes weren't triggering builds. Everything merged today is safe and publishes to the live site once it clears. No action needed unless the site is still stale tomorrow.

🏷 SPLIT A STATUS THAT'S DOING TWO JOBS. 'Local CPL only' currently means both 'a college offers this' and 'the credential exists but nobody has adopted it' — very different answers for a student. Engineering Designer is the live example: 2 credentials, 0 colleges. The visual and the spreadsheet both say so honestly, but the underlying label is still coarse. Cheapest moment to fix it is the next partner run.

⚠ 15 colleges publish NO usable counseling route. Two of them (Contra Costa, LA Harbor) publish only a mental-health inbox — the address a person would grab by eye is actively the wrong door for a credit question. Five list individual counselors with no designated contact; six are phone/form only. Each carries its source link.
